subject: Early renewal incentive + tier consolidation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medixa.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@medixa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Early renewal incentive + tier consolidation

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Based on the Q2 usage profile and the growth signal you shared, we built a short proposal that aims to: 1) simplify Medixa's footprint across two tiers into a single consolidated committed tier, 2) give you an early-renewal incentive that reduces unit cost today, and 3) provide runway protection if usage spikes unexpectedly.

High-level offer (summary):
- Co-term and commit to 12 months from signing: 12% reduction on list unit price for the consolidated tier.
- Usage anchoring: baseline set at Q2 average; usage above baseline triggers step credits (2% credits at +20% usage, 5% at +50%).
- Holdback for burst: 10% of the uplift converted to refundable credits if you exceed 150% of baseline in any month (protects against runaway costs).

Attachments: Medixa_MA_plan_v2.pdf (proposal), usage_report_Q2.csv (raw).

If that structure looks directionally right, can you confirm the procurement timeline? If procurement can sign an order within 2 weeks we can lock the 12% incentive and waive the standard admin fee. Otherwise we can offer a reduced 8% early-renewal incentive on a 30-day review cadence.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm procurement path and any legal redlines to expect
- Us: if green, we’ll produce an updated order form and route for DocuSign

Thanks — happy to hop on 15 min to walk through.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0117

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medixa.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@medixa.com>
Cc: procurement@medixa.com
Date: 2028-07-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early renewal incentive + tier consolidation

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear proposal. Quick reactions from our side:
- Consolidating tiers makes sense operationally.
- The main sticking point is the 12% up-front reduction tied to a full 12-month commit — we have seasonality and next quarter may need a spike buffer.
- The holdback/refundable-credit approach is interesting, but procurement will want clearer language on how credits are applied and timing for refunds.

Two asks before we can move to legal/procurement:
1) Can you convert the 12% up-front reduction into a split: 8% on signing + 4% delivered as monthly usage credits tied to the step thresholds? That helps our finance team from a cashflow perspective.
2) Can you provide examples of how the credits flow on the invoice (i.e., a sample invoice row)?

Looping in procurement — procurement@medixa.com — to weigh in on PO timing. I’d like to get internal alignment this week if possible.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product Ops, Medixa Health
elena.morales@medixa.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Early renewal incentive + tier consolidation — Medixa reply / procurement asks

Ben / Jonas —

Forwarding Elena’s reply — customer is asking to convert the 12% into 8% on-sign + 4% as usage credits (monthly). Procurement wants an invoice example and clearer credit application language.

My suggested concession matrix (internal):
- Option A (preferred): 12% up-front if PO signed within 14 days; credits flow as negative invoice line with 30-day settlement; waive admin fee.
- Option B (compromise): 8% up-front + 4% cumulative usage credits over the year triggered by step thresholds; credits applied monthly as account credit and visible on invoice.
- Option C (defensive): 8% up-front only, review at 90 days if usage grows >25% then apply ad-hoc credit.

I recommend we offer Option B if legal signs off on the credit wording — it helps procurement (cashflow) and keeps list price protection for us. Can you review the wording in the attached internal_pricing_matrix.xlsx and confirm legal/finance flags? If we can greenlight B I’ll prepare the order form and a sample invoice row to share with Medixa.

Also note: if procurement can’t sign within 30 days, we should revert to Option C and present that as final.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medixa.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@medixa.com>
Cc: procurement@medixa.com
Date: 2028-07-31T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early renewal incentive + tier consolidation

Naomi —

Procurement has signed off on Option B (8% on-sign + 4% monthly usage credits tied to steps). They asked legal to align the credit application language; that’s done. We attached the signed PO and our internal signer scanned it.

Next steps on your side:
- Please send an updated order form reflecting Option B and consolidated tier pricing.
- Add a sample invoice row showing the monthly deduction flow (credits applied against usage line items).
- Send to docusign (link below works for procurement).

We’re happy to move forward — procurement expects a DocuSign package today so finance can process payment on the next run.

Attached: Medixa_PO_7432.pdf (signed PO).

Thanks,
Elena
